chunks: And said: "We (affirm and) believe in the Lord of all the worlds,
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'We believe in the Lord of the worlds' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this declaration is often viewed as the archetype of sincere faith (Iman) that withstands political and social pressure, reflecting the steadfastness of the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers. The phrase 'Lord of the Worlds' (Rabb al-Alamin) underscores Allah's universal sovereignty, a concept central to Shia theological discussions on divine lordship (Rububiyyah) extending beyond mere creation to include guidance and sustenance for all existence.
